<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via PageTabsProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via newTab (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object pageActionRowNavigationExecutorToUrl), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object pageActionRowNavigationExecutorToUrl))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via actionType (literal, a string literal in ActionButtonPropsSchema; a string literal in ActionIconPropsSchema; a string literal in refuseRowUrlExecutorAlias; a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39f6812ce2f5c64985c116224750442bf824f50d` — the merge of head `f4d39d7aa5fba4817493b617f66103f385df8190` into base `d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39f6812ce2f5c64985c116224750442bf824f50d && git checkout 39f6812ce2f5c64985c116224750442bf824f50d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad f4d39d7aa5fba4817493b617f66103f385df8190 && git checkout -B drift-repro d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad && git merge --no-ff f4d39d7aa5fba4817493b617f66103f385df8190

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d889448b930bf79dd8e6d0749d51e7732d69daad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**CI red on `bb41814b8`: `Test Core (1/6)` fails in `@objectstack/driver-turso#test`.** Seat note from `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_019G5ZnRrTMiwcHG6iZM19zf` · 2026-10-13T05:04Z.

- **The failing task:** `packages/drivers/driver-turso` `pnpm run test` exited 1. Turbo then stopped the shard's other tasks: `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-knowledge` print a bare `ELIFECYCLE` and are "never reached" per `check-test-completeness`. The job log does not carry the turso test output, so the failing case is not yet named.
- **Read so far:**
  - This PR touches `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, its tests, the ledger, two D3 entries, one lint test and a generated reference page. It touches nothing in `driver-turso`.
  - `Test Core` is green on `main`'s last five completed commits (`d206d08ca` through `02bec6ca8`).
  - So it is either a flake in that package (a timing-window race there is on record, #17079) or a real interaction the spec change has with it. That is not decided yet.
- **Next:** the dev reproduces `driver-turso`'s suite on this head and names the failing case. A real interaction gets fixed in this PR. A flake gets one re-run, and a robustness fix or a filed flake card if it reproduces.
- The contract-tier review on this head is running, and the PR is not queued.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb41814b84cf204cdcb3b77a489fe69a46f7264b`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract-review subagent of `domain:spec` seat 1 (seat post #6017, account `os-warren`). Read-only. PR #23164 (card #23103; body lines `Fixes #23103`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`), judged on the net diff against `main` at the merge base `d206d08ca`: 9 files, +528 / −37. `main` has since moved to `02bec6ca8` (four commits, #23146 among them) and none of them touches a file in this PR's list, so the net diff against current `main` is the same diff. Inputs: the card body and its comments `6133636513`, `6134148885`, `6136510921`, `6138537219`, `6138578423`; ruling A+ on objectstack-ai/objectui#12191 (comment `6121792024`) with `packages/spec/src/ui/navigation-target.ts` on `main` and PRs #23076 / #23101 as its two applications; #23036's report `6137432578` and PR #23146's review `6137629159`; the PR body, file list and diff; the check-runs on this head; #23168. Producer sweeps were read on objectstack `origin/main` `02bec6ca8` and objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `1fb1ced36243`, which this PR does not move. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The four rows' `onSuccess` is `ActionSchema`'s own block, by reference — RIGHT.** `ActionSchema` is `lazySchema` over `actionObject().refine(…)…superRefine(…).transform(…)` (`action.zod.ts:2081` to `:2332` on `main`), so it is a pipe whose `.in` is the object half; the lazySchema proxy forwards the read. `.in.shape.onSuccess` is the `ZodOptional` over the `strictObject` block declared at `:1782-1807`, and `refuseUnopenableOnSuccessNavigate` sits on that block, not on the action. `.unwrap()` returns that instance; each row wraps it in a fresh `.optional().describe(…)` whose inner type is the same object, which the identity pin asserts with `toBe`. So the block's whole judgement rides along: the scheme set through `navigationTargetRefusal`, the eight rename prescriptions (`redirectUrl` / `url` / `to` / `route` / `path` / `target` / `navigateTo` / `href` onto `navigate`), the closed `openIn` with its `'new-tab'` message and `'self'` default. The verdict-parity pin compares ten probes against `ActionSchema`'s own answer, path-relative. `action.zod.ts` is not in the file list; `actionOnSuccessBlock` is module-private and `ActionSchema` was already barrel-exported, so no export moves. No second shape and no second URL grammar: the diff carries no scheme literal, and the one precedent it follows is `component.zod.ts:7939` (`FormFieldSchema`'s `.in.shape`). The parsed state gains `openIn: 'self'` when omitted; the four `*Parsed` TSDocs and the changeset say so, and the runner reads only `block.openIn === 'newTab'` (pin `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:1705`), so no behaviour moves. The action-level rules about `onSuccess` (only beside `api` / `script`; not beside `opensInNewTab`) are rightly not carried: they refine the action, whose `type` is closed, and the row's executor is open; the accessor's TSDoc records this.

2. **The executor key stays open and refuses only `'navigation'` — RIGHT, within the triage direction and ruling A+, and not a fork for the decision box.** The triage direction (`6134148885`) names a goal and a mechanism: "the rows' executor key takes the declared action-type set, so a navigation-type row is judged the way a `url` row is". The mechanism was falsified by measurement, and I confirmed every reading. Closing the key to `ActionType` (`action.zod.ts:559`, the six built-ins) would refuse: the console's own registered handlers at the pin, `navigate_create` and `navigate_edit` (`app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:521`, `:533`), `crud_success` and `dialog_cancel` (`:488`, `:495`), `create`, `delete`, `navigate`, `refresh` (`app-shell/src/hooks/useObjectActions.ts:98-129`); this package's released CHANGELOG prescription `actionType: 'navigate_edit'` (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:1708`); the landed spec pins that write `type: 'navigate_edit'` members (`component-action-member-params-array-only.pin.test.ts:63`, `:85`, `:114`, `:138`; `component-report-items-action-members-typed.pin.test.ts:325`); objectui's own docs (`content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md:79`, `:132`; `packages/app-shell/README.md:977`, each `"actionType": "navigate_create"`); and the rows' own published `.describe()`, "a handler registered under another name is dispatched too". That is the door narrower than the runner which `navigation-target.ts`'s header names as the trap, and it is a second, undeclared retirement, outside the card. The other live reading, judging `target` on `'navigation'` as a url, would encode a renderer-local alias as accepted vocabulary, which Prime Directive #12 forbids when no producer needs it. Refusing the alias at the key with the lossless rename is the one reading that meets the direction's goal (a `'navigation'` row no longer admits a target the click refuses; after the rename its `target` is judged as a `url` row's) under both directives, and it is one of the two shapes the folded position `6133636513` itself offered ("so `'navigation'` is refused or normalised at parse"). A2's first half holds too: `ACTION_NODE_ALIASES` (`type` to `actionType`, `visibleWhen` / `visibility` to `visible`) and `ACTION_TARGET_ALIASES` (`url` / `endpoint` / `path` / `href` to `target`) alias keys, so the refinement reads the raw executor value. The overturning is written in the PR body with the corpus readings and acknowledged on the card (report, ACCEPT), which is the review checklist's form for a measured correction of a dispatch premise. Ruling A+ decides the scheme set and the stated-once principle; it says nothing about executor vocabulary, and nothing here departs from it. The patch round below keeps this reading.

3. **No value a real producer writes today is refused.** Objectstack `origin/main` `02bec6ca8`: no page action row in `examples/`, `content/docs/` or `skills/` writes an `onSuccess` object (every hit is a React `onSuccess` prop or a release note) and none writes a `'navigation'` executor (the only hits are CHANGELOG prose and `action.zod.ts` comments); `platform-objects`' generated `onSuccess` entries are form labels, not rows. Objectui at `1fb1ced36243`: the row tests write `{ navigate: '/app/records/${result.id}', openIn: 'newTab' }` and `{ navigate: '/app/records/${result.id}' }` (`action-button-icon-inputs-11168.test.tsx:475`, `:481`), both admitted; `{ type: 'notify' }` is on a runner `ActionDef` (`consoleServerAction.test.tsx:416`), not a row; every `type: 'navigation'` is an `element:button` inline action or a runner / hook test; `action-button.tsx:376` forwards `onSuccess` whole. Host-handler names stay accepted and the `navigate_edit` control is pinned. cloud, hotcrm and deployed metadata are NOT MEASURED, as declared.

4. **The props gate (A3) — RIGHT.** `validateComponentProps` parses `properties` against the same `ComponentPropsMap` rows, so both refusals reach `os validate` with no lint code change; the lint file pins path and first sentence for all four rows, plus the accepted controls. The finding is a `component-props-invalid` warning, that gate's one tier, and the changeset says "reports", which is the honest verb.

5. **The declared rider — RIGHT.** The `page:tabs` item `visibleWhen` TSDoc now says the component-node evaluator mounts no `data` root, citing `containers.tsx:642-649` at `1fb1ced36243`; at the pin those lines build `new ExpressionEvaluator({ …row, …predicateScope, current_user, record: recordData, data: recordData, page })`, and `react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:665-676` (`configEvaluationScope`) builds `{ …predicateScope, current_user, record?, page }` with no `data`, the absence recorded at `:1194`. The `.describe()` parenthetical "(the component-node evaluator mounts no `data` root)" states the same fact and republishes at `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx:1578`; its cross-reference to `PageComponentSchema.visibleWhen` resolves on `main` since `02bec6ca8`. The addendum's TSDoc-face assertion in `expression-scope-data-root.pin.test.ts` was not added because the file did not exist at this PR's base; it exists on `main` now, so the patch round may add the one line, and #23146's escalation condition (a card if the rider were absent) is not triggered.

6. **The ledger and the pin ledger — RIGHT.** `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains exactly the four sites `build-schemas` derives (`ui/ActionButtonProps` and `ui/ActionIconProps` `onSuccess`; `ui/ActionGroupProps` and `ui/ActionMenuProps` `actions.element.onSuccess`), header 232 / 756, no site removed. `component-props-unknown-members.pin.test.ts` drops `onSuccess` from its `runner` ledger, which its §1 second half would otherwise refuse as a line that outlived its member.

7. **Describe text, TSDoc and the regenerated reference page — RIGHT.** Each key states the set it enforces, the describe strings and refusal messages carry no tracker number, and `component.mdx` is generated output. The published input types `ActionButtonProps['onSuccess']` and siblings narrow from `unknown` to the block's input type, which is the declared narrowing; `Type Check · source gates` (the `check:api-surface` / `check:authorable-surface` / `check:docs` lane) is success on this head.

8. **One defect the diff writes into shipped source — WRONG, owed in the patch round.** The new clause in `refuseUnopenableRowUrlTarget`'s docblock (`component.zod.ts`, head, in the hunk at old `:3971`): "the url executor's alias spelling `'navigation'` is refused at the executor key, so no row reaches the url navigator with its `target` unjudged". At the pin a row with no executor key and `name: 'url'` or `'navigation'` reaches `executeUrl` / `executeNavigation` with its `target` unjudged: `ActionRunner.execute` reads `action.type || action.actionType || action.name` (`:1265`) and `action-button.tsx:286` forwards `type: schema.actionType`. The dev measured exactly this (out-of-scope finding 1) and the seat filed it as #23168, so the sentence is known false as written. `@objectstack/spec` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so a TSDoc face is a published face, and a false one this round writes is fixed this round: qualify the clause to the executor key (the absent-key `name` leg is #23168's).

### ② Semver level

- **Level and declaration — RIGHT.** `.changeset/23103-page-action-row-on-success-and-executor.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the marker `adr-0087: registered` naming `ui-page-action-row-on-success-shape-closed` and `ui-page-action-row-navigation-executor-refused`; the PR body's second line and the claim `6136510921` declare the same arm. The arm is right: two accept sets narrow and nothing authorable is added. `minor` with the banner is what ADR-0087's ratified launch-window section states for a pre-GA metadata-facing break, in the form the family's two landed changesets took. The FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are present; no `content/docs/releases/` page and no `CHANGELOG.md` is edited. `Check Changeset`, which runs `check-adr-0087-registration`, is success on this head.
- **The two D3 entries — well-formed.** Both carry `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` in the shape of the landed `18.ui-page-action-row-url-target-scheme-set-closed.ts`, name no npm or protocol version, and carry no `conversionIds`.
- **`ui-page-action-row-on-success-shape-closed` — RIGHT as D3 only.** A refused `navigate` has no lossless target (the entry says so: a bare `tasks/${result.id}` may mean either rooted form, and a `tel:` or `javascript:` hop has no admitted equivalent), so the chain owes a judgment, not a rewrite.
- **`ui-page-action-row-navigation-executor-refused` — WRONG as a disposition, and the reason this record fails.** The leg is a lossless rename, as the entry itself states ("The rename is lossless on a row"), on metadata the conversion chain already walks: `mapPageComponents` reaches `regions[].components[]`, `slots` and the containers (`conversions/registry.ts:5126`), and the landed `page.component.element:button.action.params` conversion (`:5581`) rewrites a page component's `properties` through it. ADR-0087's ratified launch-window section requires that "every such break must land as a chain step (a `retiredFromLoadPath` conversion when lossless, and one D3 semantic entry per retirement family in every case; D2 carries the mechanical data repair only) in the same release", and says the exemption "covers the window only — never the chain"; its cost paragraph says the conversion entry is the point, the producer paying for the break. The entry's stated reason for registering none, "the authored census finds no page action row writing `'navigation'` in this repository or in objectui", is the condition under which every retirement ships and is what the chain exists for; the family's own sibling entry says so of itself ("the entry is owed for targets authored outside them"), and deployed metadata is NOT MEASURED. The lane's practice matches the ADR: every landed D3 entry that calls its change lossless either has its D2 (`18.action-aria-retired`, `18.chart-config-aria-retired`, `18.connector-error-mapping-retired`, `18.api-endpoint-cache-ttl-unit-in-key`) or names a source the chain cannot rewrite (`18.action-engine-facade-find-query-envelope`: a handler's TypeScript); none skips a D2 on a census. What a stored row needs it for: a page's `properties` is not parsed on the load path (`PageComponentSchema.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, `page.zod.ts:591`), so a stored `'navigation'` row keeps working only while objectui's runner keeps the alias, and the entry's own startup-scope reasoning expects that alias to retire with no bridge; the chain replayed on `sys_metadata` rows (`applyConversionsToStoredItem`, ADR-0087 addendum) and by `os migrate meta --write` is what carries deployed rows across that. The claim's file surface listed "the ADR-0087 D3 entry or entries" when the key was expected to close to a set, a non-lossless change; once the mechanism became a lossless alias refusal, the ADR's lossless branch applies, and the ADR outranks the claim's list. **Owed in the patch round:** one `MetadataConversion` in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, inserted in its header's order), `retiredFromLoadPath: true` and `retiredAfter` set to the current package label, walking `mapPageComponents` to rename the executor value `'navigation'` to `'url'` on `action:button` / `action:icon` `properties.actionType` and on `action:group` / `action:menu` `properties.actions[].type`, copy-on-write and idempotent, with a disjoint fixture pair; `conversionIds` naming it on the D3 entry, whose `reason` then stops saying no conversion is registered; and the changeset's "the rewrite is by hand" sentence corrected for this leg. The `spec-property-retirement` skill §3 is the kit (three independent obligations: registry entry where a key retires, conversion, D3 entry; for a rename `retiredFromLoadPath: true` means no alias window, deliberately).

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report `6138537219` lists `open_questions: []`, four `deviations` and three `out_of_scope_findings`; the ACCEPT `6138578423` names three report items. Each answered:

- **A1 held — confirmed.** The three rows declared `onSuccess: z.unknown().optional()` at the base (the diff's removed lines), and the runner reads a row's forwarded `onSuccess` only through `handlePostExecution` (`:1531`, after every executor and after a host handler at `:1394`), `readOnSuccessNavigation` (`:2532-2537`: a non-array object with a non-empty string `navigate`) and `navigateOnSuccess` (`:1676-1711`: interpolate, classify, `openIn === 'newTab'`). No key outside the block is read, so one block serves both doors with no fork.
- **A2 partly falsified — confirmed, and the resulting choice judged in ① item 2.** The runner's built-in table (`:1145-1150`) is the spec's six plus `navigation`, its only url-like alias; `executeNavigation` (`:2221-2228`) reads `to || target || redirect` and hands off to `navigateTo`, the navigator `executeUrl` calls. The correction is public on the card; no card body carries the falsified mechanism (it lives in the triage comment and the claim), so no follow-up card is owed for it.
- **A3 held** — the lint pins (① item 4).
- **The census** — read and extended (① item 3); the NOT MEASURED set is accepted as declared.
- **The rider** — ① item 5.
- **Deviations.** (1) The rider: answered. (2) Files beyond the claim's literal list, `component-props-unknown-members.pin.test.ts` and the new spec test: both declared, both consequences of the change. (3) Base and merge: merge base `d206d08ca` verified; `main` has moved to `02bec6ca8` touching none of these nine files. (4) The two process notes (a stopped mis-spelled run; a probe script copied into `packages/lint` and deleted): no diff effect, and the file list shows no stray file.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1, the runner's `name` leg** — carried by #23168, which I read: it states the measurement (0 findings for `{ name: 'url', target: 'javascript:alert(1)' }` and for `name: 'navigation'`; 1 for the `actionType: 'url'` control) and leaves the contract choice to its claim. Right as filed. The TSDoc clause in ① item 8 is the same gap written as a guarantee; it is fixed here, and #23168 decides the rest.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2, a `url` or host-handler row with an `onSuccess` navigates twice** — read from source, not executed; a contract question for its own card, as the dev says. The ACCEPT names #23168 as its carrier, but #23168's body as filed carries no such line, so on the record it is noted, not filed: the seat adds the line to #23168 or files it. Not a condition of this verdict.
